angles_unseen: The verbatim metric is too strict to be a product metric: 62% exact against 94% normalised means most 'failures' are whitespace, and a packet built on the exact metric would throw away correct values. The citation check must normalise whitespace and punctuation before it decides anything.

The model returns the literal string `null` as a value at 0.908 and 0.787 confidence, both above the 0.6 gate. It means 'no deposit stated', but as delivered it renders `Security Deposit: null` in a packet. That is a one-line client filter, and it must exist before any packet ships.

EDGAR full-text search is not a lease corpus: of the first four 'lease' hits, one was a letter about leases, one an equipment lease and one a bond-financed lease. A product ingesting customer documents is unaffected; a product mining public filings needs a document-type gate before extraction, and that gate is itself a model job.

The 50% escalation is concentrated in the judgement questions (`tenant may terminate early`, `term over five years`), not the literal fields. Literal extraction is near-solved; the escalation cost sits exactly where a lease admin bills their time.
conditions: Ship literal fields only, each with a citation that survives whitespace normalisation, and compute derived fields in code from those literals.
Filter the literal string `null` (and `NULL`, `N/A`, `none`) before a value reaches the packet; treat it as absence.
Do not price the abstract on the decision layer: 50% of judgement questions escalate, and that is the paralegal time the product is supposed to replace.
Publish the escalation rate per field, not per document, because it is the per-field rate that tells a buyer what they are still paying for.
